rule: Read the KEGG_Pathway field for every annotated protein in each genome.
Split comma-separated annotations and accept only exact tokens matching (ko|map)[0-9]{5}.
Remove the ko/map prefix and retain the five-digit pathway identifier; paired aliases such as ko00010 and map00010 collapse to one identifier.
Store canonical identifiers as a set for each protein so duplicate aliases are counted once.
Count proteins assigned to each canonical pathway identifier within each genome.
Set pathway presence to 1 when at least one annotated protein supports the identifier, otherwise 0; no pathway-completeness threshold was imposed.
Take the union across the frozen 1,000-genome cohort, yielding 264 canonical pathway-associated features.
Classify the 264 features with the recorded KEGG ontology decision table and retain 115 bacterial-relevant features for inferential analyses.
Features represent pathway-associated ortholog evidence, not complete pathway reconstruction, pathway activity, or flux.
